subject.title: CLI startup preflight can corrupt the live state DB while a gateway is running — health-check commands caused "database disk image is malformed" (2026.6.6, macOS); vanilla SQLite control does NOT reproduce

question: Should OpenClaw solve this by making CLI diagnostics strictly RPC-first/no-maintenance when a gateway owns the shared state DB, or by adding a broader single-writer lease for all non-gateway openers?
rationale: Both paths affect shared SQLite ownership, CLI observability, doctor migrations, and recovery behavior, so automation should not choose the permanent product boundary without maintainer intent.

options.title: RPC-first diagnostics with no-maintenance fallback
options.body: Prefer Gateway RPC for status/health/stability and make any direct CLI fallback read-only with no WAL or migration side effects while a gateway is active.

options.title: Gateway-owned single-writer lease
options.body: Add a broader lease/sentinel so non-gateway processes refuse read-write state DB access or WAL maintenance while the gateway owns the store.

options.title: Wait for deterministic live repro
options.body: Keep current opener behavior and request a runtime-specific harness first, accepting ongoing production corruption risk until the race is reproduced.

recommendation.title: RPC-first diagnostics with no-maintenance fallback
recommendation.body: Prefer Gateway RPC for status/health/stability and make any direct CLI fallback read-only with no WAL or migration side effects while a gateway is active.

likelyOwner.reason: Broad runtime-state SQLite ownership traces to PR #78595 and the decision is an architecture/product boundary rather than a local line fix.
